replies.text: {"verdicts":[{"id":"T1","keep":true,"reason":"Design states fetcher downloads arbitrary URL from inside VPC next to metadata service; classic SSRF attack supported."},{"id":"T2","keep":true,"reason":"Distinct attack via non-HTTP schemes reading local files, different target and fix than network SSRF."},{"id":"T3","keep":true,"reason":"Design names no authentication for the URL-accepting endpoint; unauthenticated abuse and lack of attribution is concrete."},{"id":"T4","keep":true,"reason":"Design says service downloads and resizes attacker-chosen images; decompression/oversize resource exhaustion is concrete."},{"id":"T5","keep":true,"reason":"Redirect/DNS rebinding bypass of validation is a distinct attack path on the described fetcher."},{"id":"T6","keep":false,"reason":"Same attacker using fetcher's in-VPC position to reach internal endpoints; restates T1's confused-deputy attack.","duplicateOf":"T1"},{"id":"T7","keep":true,"reason":"Distinct harm: outbound proxy abuse against third parties, reputation/egress damage, not internal disclosure or memory exhaustion."}]}
